newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Templeton ventures into Switzerland to lure funds.
newsitem.headline: Templeton ventures into Switzerland to lure funds.

text.p: Emerging Market Funds, among the world's biggest investment groups with more than $14 billion under management, announced plans on Friday to open up in Switzerland to tap an ever-rising mountain of cash.
The company's president, world emerging markets guru Mark Mobius, said the new office in Zurich was likely to become operational in the coming days.
Asked why Switzerland, Mobius said: "Money money money."

"We see more money coming into Switzerland from European and emerging markets. Important companies are here, important investors are here, important funds are here. It makes an awful lot of sense to be here."

Templeton is a leading player on emerging markets, whose share in the world market capitalisation has soared from just four percent in 1981 to more than 14 percent in 1996 as countries open up their markets and reform their economies.
Templeton says this share will grow to 25 percent by 2000.

Switzerland is a leading asset management centre with an estimated 40 percent of the wealth of the world's super-rich. Swiss banks estimate that some $1.8 trillion in assets is under management in Switzerland.

Templeton, already with offices in Hong Kong, Singapore, Vietnam, India, United Arab Emirates, South Africa, Argentina, Brazil, Poland and Russia, is the latest newcomer to the Swiss market where competition is growing.
In addition to leading Swiss banks, foreign groups selling mutual funds here include Fidelity, Flemings, Citibank and Nomura. The bulk of their clients are foreign investors.
"We hope to become significant players on the Swiss market," Mobius said. "It is very difficult to replace Switzerland. You have services, multi-lingual people, experience and all these banks here."

Secretive Swiss banks do not publish data on the volume of assets in Switzerland, but bankers estimate that the volume of net cash flows grew by 10-15 percent in the first quarter of the year thanks to both performance of markets which have offered dizzying returns so far this year as well as new money.
